title: Pasqal Leads European Defence Fund Project on Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
excerpt: Pasqal leads CoPaNA, a European Defence Fund project with ParityQC and Thales Nederland to advance fault-tolerant quantum computing using neutral atoms.
content:
Insider Brief

  • Pasqal is coordinating CoPaNA, a three-year European Defence Fund project with ParityQC and Thales Nederland to advance fault-tolerant quantum computing using neutral-atom hardware.
  • The consortium will work on quantum error correction, hardware-software integration and the requirements for potential defence and cybersecurity applications.
  • The project aims to develop a blueprint for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing and supports Europe’s efforts to build sovereign quantum capabilities.

PRESS RELEASE — Pasqal (Nasdaq: PSQL), a global leader in neutral-atom quantum computing, today announced the public launch of CoPaNA (Concatenated Parity codes on Neutral Atoms), a three-year research project selected under the European Defence Fund (EDF) 2025 call and coordinated by Pasqal. Together with ParityQC (Austria) and Thales Nederland (Netherlands), Pasqal will work to advance the development of scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC).

Fault tolerance is the next frontier of quantum computing. To tackle the most demanding problems, quantum computers must detect and correct their own errors at scale. CoPaNA brings together advances in quantum error correction and neutral-atom hardware to address this challenge, while exploring future applications in defense relevant simulations and cybersecurity. The project aims to develop a blueprint for scalable FTQC, combining research into quantum error correction, hardware-software integration and the technical requirements of potential defense applications.

The project is aligned with the 2025 EU Quantum Strategy and Europe’s ambition to secure sovereign access to next-generation computing capabilities. It also contributes to the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base by developing dual-use quantum technologies with European partners.

The consortium builds on the complementary strengths of its three members. ParityQC brings its expertise in quantum error-correcting codes and architectures, Pasqal leads the hardware and experimental work on its neutral-atom quantum processing unit (QPU), and Thales Nederland identifies the defense applications where these capabilities could make a difference and estimates the resources needed to run them on a fault-tolerant machine.

Pasqal has already outlined its public roadmap toward fault-tolerant quantum computing, targeting early FTQC capabilities in 2029. CoPaNA complements this roadmap by exploring how future FTQC systems could support applications in defense and cybersecurity. The project also reflects Pasqal’s commitment to advancing dual-use quantum technologies through European industrial and research collaboration.

The project is presented today at “Quantum Computing as a Strategic Technology in Defence and Security,” a public event in Innsbruck bringing together governments, EU institutions and industry to discuss the industrial and policy levers necessary to unlock the full potential of quantum computing for Europe’s defense and security. On November 26, Pasqal will also deliver a keynote on CoPaNA and quantum computing dual-use applications at the European Defence Agency (EDA) technical workshop “Quantum Technologies for Defence” in Athens, gathering experts from industry, national ministries and academia.

“Fault-tolerant quantum computing will redraw global technological and strategic maps, just as AI is doing today,” said Wasiq Bokhari, CEO of Pasqal. “CoPaNA brings together European leaders’ expertise in hardware, quantum error correction and defense systems to address some of the key technological challenges on the path to scalable quantum computing. By coordinating this initiative, Pasqal is helping build the sovereign quantum capabilities Europe needs to strengthen its defense and security, while advancing technologies with applications far beyond the defense sector.”

“Building a scalable quantum computer is, first and foremost, an architecture challenge. Fault tolerance does not come from hardware alone but from the way the entire system is designed,” said Wolfgang Lechner, Co-CEO of ParityQC. “Within CoPaNA, ParityQC contributes the architecture and quantum error correction these machines need to become reliable at scale,” added Magdalena Hauser Co-CEO of ParityQC.

“To function in a rapidly evolving threat landscape, future defense systems will need to process an unprecedented flow of data in real time. Quantum computing has the potential to provide the processing power we will require to maintain situational awareness, enabling operators to continue making fast, well-informed decisions. Through CoPaNA, we are exploring how this technology can contribute to Europe’s future defense capabilities.” said Koen ten Hove, Chief Technical Officer of Thales Nederland.
